findings.summary: Save.load() runs the version-1 migration shim outside the try/catch that guards JSON.parse, so a valid-JSON-but-wrong-typed v1 save (e.g. {"version":1,"settings":"x"}) makes the ??=/||= inits throw (strict-mode assignment on a primitive), aborting boot to a black screen before createEngine runs.

The engine resizes the canvas backing store only when clientWidth/clientHeight change, so a devicePixelRatio change (browser zoom or a monitor handoff at the booth) with an unchanged CSS size leaves the backing store at the old DPR scale, yielding a blurry / wrongly-scaled canvas.

submitKiosk pushes a failed submission into the allin-pending localStorage queue but nothing ever re-submits or flushes that queue, so a visitor's idea captured during a server outage stays stranded on the booth machine and never reaches the build queue.

Save_hasProgress() reads the allin-arcade-save-v1 key directly and treats any truthy non-object 'completed' (e.g. a string) as progress, enabling Continue and miscounting cleared levels; it also parses the same JSON twice.

serve.py's path-containment check compares against os.path.normpath(ROOT + os.sep), which carries no trailing separator, so a sibling directory whose name begins with the root name (e.g. /…/repo-evil/…) would also pass the startswith guard.

/api/submit silently truncates the request body to 64KB via min(Content-Length, 64000), so a legitimate long prompt is cut off and rejected as 'bad json'; a missing Content-Length reads 0 bytes and also returns 400.

The rAF loop clamps dt to 0.05 (good) but there is no visibilitychange listener anywhere; while a booth tab is hidden the loop pauses and the audio setInterval(pump,60) keeps scheduling against real-time ac.currentTime, and on resume the first frame receives a large-but-clamped dt, with no guard against a negative (now-last).

rewind.js schedules a setTimeout in create() with no clearTimeout on level exit, so exiting the level before ~350ms lets beatOnce fire against a torn-down closure, and rapid re-entry stacks duplicate timers.

ensure() calls ac.resume() without awaiting/catching it, so if it runs outside a recognised user gesture (e.g. playMusic at boot via ?level=) the returned promise can reject as an unhandled rejection; the gesture unlock itself (pointerdown/keydown) is correct.
_startFile appends one <audio> element to document.body per mood and never removes it, so fileEls accumulates up to ~9 detached-but-present elements for the whole app lifetime.

No genre implements the engine's exit() hook and the shared playScene has no cleanup, so any module-level listener/cache/timer a genre ever registers is never torn down on level change; today the per-level state is recreated inside each create() closure so gameplay does not leak, but the missing exit() is a latent leak.

The maze genres push to window.__MAZE_RUNS__ (initialised once, never reset) and rewrite window.__TEST_API__ in create(); the thumbnail hot-import path (app.js) can re-run create() and stomp __TEST_API__ mid-playtest — test-harness only.
/api/submit appends to submissions/pending.jsonl with no rotation or cap, so the pending queue grows unboundedly over a long booth session (drained only by an external claimant process).
